answer: Make settlement fees fall with each identity's own audited lifetime volume: a fresh key pays 8% per job, while an agent that has spent a year pricing ferrous scrap freight and karst groundwater surveys pays 1%. The fee bracket is bound to that key's cipher-signed history and can't be pooled or transferred, so a farm that splits its work across clones keeps every clone stuck in the costly bracket and bleeds margin on each job.
